title: What stops working when traffic bypasses SSL/TLS inspection

checks.do: Whether the traffic matched a Do Not Inspect rule, before reading a content feature's own policy when it missed something on HTTPS.

dependent-features.statement: These ZIA security features need decrypted traffic to work on encrypted transactions: Anti-Virus/Malware, Cloud Sandbox, Advanced Threat Prevention, Isolation, Data Loss Prevention, File Type Control, Inline CASB and the Intrusion Prevention System.

quotes: security features require SSL inspection to work on encrypted transactions.

uninspected-blind.statement: Zscaler cannot see inside uninspected traffic, so embedded threats, inbound or outbound, are not detected.

quotes: Zscaler cannot see inside uninspected traffic, meaning any embedded threats (inbound or outbound) are not detected.

check-ssl-first.statement: When a dependent feature missed something on HTTPS, check whether the traffic matched a Do Not Inspect rule before looking at the feature's own policy.
check-ssl-first.conditions: Diagnostic advice following from the dependency: no source states the troubleshooting order.

evaluate-variant-keeps-domain-checks.statement: On Do Not Inspect with Evaluate Other Policies, URL Filtering and Cloud App Control still evaluate the destination domain, so a block on the domain fires while path-, method- and payload-based rules do not; Do Not Inspect with Bypass Other Policies skips both entirely.
evaluate-variant-keeps-domain-checks.conditions: not-inspected-domain-only names URL Filtering for the Evaluate variant; the Cloud App Control half assumes the domain-level first pass (first-pass-on-domain) applies to it equally.

per-feature-bypass-effects.title: What each dependent feature does on bypassed HTTPS traffic
per-feature-bypass-effects.detail: Unverified legacy statement: DLP (Web, Inline CASB, Endpoint DLP sync) 'completely ineffective for HTTPS traffic'; Sandbox 'does not see files delivered over bypassed traffic'; Malware Protection 'can't scan payloads; reduced to URL/reputation matching only'; File Type Control 'MIME-type sniffing falls back to host/path heuristics; reliability drops'; ATP content-based rules 'Known-bad-URL still matches; deep-content detection doesn't'. The captured guide says only that these features require inspection. The ATP known-bad-URL part is supported by the pipeline's first-pass claims. Capturing each feature's help page would settle the rest.
